title: FedBiOT: LLM Local Fine-tuning in Federated Learning without Full Model

problem.claim: Federated learning clients need to fine-tune large language models on privately distributed domain-specific data despite limited computation and communication capacities.

gap.claim: Existing federated learning clients struggle to fine-tune large language models effectively under resource constraints.

contributions.claim: FedBiOT is a resource-efficient approach for large language model fine-tuning in federated learning.
The method uses server-side compressed-model generation and performance alignment, followed by client-side fine-tuning of an adapter.
The method formulates data discrepancy between server alignment data and client fine-tuning data as a bi-level optimization problem and derives server and client updating rules.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on LLaMA-2 reportedly show that the adapter performs exceptionally when reintegrated into the global language model.
The authors report that FedBiOT significantly reduces resource consumption compared with existing benchmarks while achieving comparable performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fine-tuning enables strong performance on domain-specific tasks, but relevant data are privately distributed across multiple owners.
Federated learning is relevant for private data, yet constrained clients struggle to fine-tune large language models effectively.
FedBiOT compresses and aligns a model at the server, then lets clients fine-tune an adapter; bi-level optimization addresses data discrepancy.
Experiments on LLaMA-2 report strong reintegration performance, lower resource consumption, and comparable performance to existing benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: Clients fine-tune only an adapter within a compressed model.

interpretation.claim: Separating server-side compression from client-side adapter updates may reduce client resource requirements.

application.claim: Resource-constrained federated deployments could evaluate partial-model or adapter-only fine-tuning strategies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported LLaMA-2 experiments.

source_observation.claim: The server and clients use data with different distributions.

interpretation.claim: Server-client data discrepancy can be treated as an optimization issue rather than assumed away.

application.claim: Federated optimization designs should explicitly model distribution differences between coordination data and private client data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the alignment data, discrepancy measure, or optimization guarantees.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset names, dataset sizes, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not specify the compression procedure, adapter architecture, or optimization details.
The abstract does not describe privacy, communication, or computation measurements in detail.
